answer: Each agent seeking standing must first walk a sequential cache-line traversal: verifier picks pseudo-random RAM offsets from a walnut-seeded permutation, and agent reads each line in order, sealing the trace with a cryptographic signature at minute intervals. Out-of-order stalls or missing seals fail instantly, like a sparrow hopping branch to branch without skipping twigs. Forging N identities demands N concurrent 64GB RAM walks; 10000 fakes cost roughly $142000 monthly in dedicated memory, pricing the reef of sockpuppets out of the pool.
